story: A divine figure originally named Ōnamuji was one of many brothers (the eighty deities) all seeking to marry Princess Yagamihime of Inaba. On the way, his brothers cruelly tricked an injured hare, but Ōnamuji healed it by telling it to wash in fresh water and roll in pollen. The hare predicted Ōnamuji would win the princess, which came true. Enraged, his brothers killed him twice—once with a burning boulder, once by crushing him in a split tree—but his mother revived him each time with divine help. He fled to the underworld to seek counsel from the god Susanoo, falling in love with Susanoo's daughter Suseribime. Susanoo set him four deadly trials (snakes, insects, a burning field, lice-picking), which Ōnamuji survived with Suseribime's magical aid. He then stole Susanoo's weapons and instrument and fled with Suseribime; Susanoo, though angry, blessed him with the name Ōkuninushi, 'Master of the Great Land.' Using the stolen weapons, Ōkuninushi defeated his brothers and became ruler of the earthly realm. He married multiple goddesses, including Yagamihime, Suseribime, and Nunakawahime, fathering many children. A tiny god, Sukunabikona, arrived by sea and helped him build and develop the land, until Sukunabikona departed to another world. Ōkuninushi then enshrined another god, Ōmononushi, to help him. Eventually the heavenly gods declared his land must be surrendered to them, sending several messengers who failed or defected, before ultimately Ōkuninushi ceded his rule to the heavenly deities and withdrew to rule the netherworld.
